abstract: A US Census Bureau America Counts story analysing six months of Business Trends and Outlook Survey data on business AI use, from December 2025 to May 2026. Its importance to this corpus is not the headline adoption rate but a methodological disclosure buried in the text: Census revised the wording of its core AI-use question in November 2025, broadening it from AI used in producing goods or services to AI used in any business function. That change sits inside the window this site plots as a single continuous adoption series, and it means part of the observed rise in 2025-2026 is definitional rather than behavioural.
keyFindings: The question changed: "Originally framed around AI use ‘in producing goods or services,’ rather than to carry out simple tasks like drafting emails, the Census Bureau revised the wording last November to ask businesses whether they were using AI ‘in any business function.’"
The revision took effect on November 17, 2025, when "BTOS began collecting data for its second AI supplement and revised the core AI use questions."
"The BTOS data (December 2025 to May 2026) show that overall AI usage hovered between 17% and 20%" with "between 20% and 23% of businesses expected to be using it in the next six months."
"the AI use rates in the Information (39.7%) and Finance and Insurance (33.9%) sectors were both higher than the national rate (19.8%)" as of May 3, 2026.

Adoption rises steeply with firm size: "37% of firms with at least 250 employees reported using AI in their business operations"; "32% of firms with 100 to 249 employees said they used AI"; "Less than 20% of firms with four or fewer employees reported using AI."
Reference period: "We reviewed the most recent six months of BTOS data collected from December 14, 2025 to May 3, 2026 to analyze trends in AI business usage."
methodology: Analysis of the Census Bureau's Business Trends and Outlook Survey, a biweekly panel of US businesses, covering waves collected December 14, 2025 to May 3, 2026. AI use is self-reported by firms for a two-week reference period. Results are broken out by NAICS sector and by employment size class. The core AI-use question was revised effective November 17, 2025 alongside the launch of the survey's second AI supplement.
qualifiers: This source is ingested primarily as a measurement caveat rather than for its point estimates. The November 2025 wording change is a genuine structural break in the series this site plots: the pre-break question asked only about AI used in producing goods or services, while the post-break question captures any business function including drafting emails and other administrative uses that the earlier framing explicitly excluded. The later question is broader by construction, so the apparent near-doubling from roughly 10% in mid-2025 to the high teens by December 2025 conflates diffusion with redefinition and cannot be decomposed from published aggregates. Because the AI adoption graph uses an aggregation method of latest, the current headline value is drawn entirely from the post-break definition. BTOS remains self-reported with no verification of what firms count as AI use, and the two-week reference window means the measure is sensitive to intermittent rather than sustained use.
